# Gupta and Larson (1979), 12 point-retention regressions for United States soils.

## Source

Gupta, S. C., & Larson, W. E. (1979). Estimating soil water retention characteristics from particle size distribution, organic matter percent, and bulk density. Water Resources Research, 15(6), 1633-1635.

[DOI: 10.1029/WR015i006p01633](https://doi.org/10.1029/WR015i006p01633)

## Scope

**Territory:** Eastern and central United States; external comparison used Missouri soils.

**Dataset:** Regression data from artificially packed cores of 43 soil materials, including 13 agricultural soils; predictions were compared with 61 Missouri soils.

## Functions

### `calc_ptf_gupta1979`

Estimate volumetric water contents at 12 matric potentials.

**Status:** `implemented`

**Prediction target:** Volumetric water content at matric potentials from -0.04 to -15 bar.

**Models:** $h(\theta)$ — Twelve point-specific multiple linear regressions

#### Inputs

| Name | Type | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sand` | `number` | % | 5 <= value <= 98 | Sand content by mass for particles from 2.0 to 0.05 mm. |
| `silt` | `number` | % | 1 <= value <= 72 | Silt content by mass for particles from 0.05 to 0.002 mm. |
| `clay` | `number` | % | 0 <= value <= 65 | Clay content by mass for particles smaller than 0.002 mm. |
| `organic_matter` | `number` | % | 0 <= value <= 23 | Soil organic matter content by mass. |
| `bulk_density` | `number` | g/cm^3 | 0.74 <= value <= 1.74 | Dry bulk density of the packed soil core. |

#### Outputs

| Name | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theta_40_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -0.04 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_70_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -0.07 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_100_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -0.10 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_200_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -0.20 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_330_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -0.33 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_600_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -0.60 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_1000_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -1.0 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_2000_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -2.0 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_4000_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -4.0 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_7000_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -7.0 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_10000_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -10.0 bar matric potential. |
| `theta_15000_cm` | cm^3/cm^3 | — | Volumetric water content at -15.0 bar matric potential. |

!!! note

    Sand, silt, and clay percentages must sum to 100.

!!! note

    Output field names use the pressure-head labels adopted by USDA-ARS CalcPTF for the article's corresponding bar-valued matric potentials.

!!! warning

    Avoid extrapolation beyond the source ranges for sand, silt, clay, organic matter, and bulk density.
